title: Redstrike Flow Context
description: Structured application state model emitted by the flow-context feeder and consumed by business-logic / race-condition / auth-bypass / idor — plus the navigation plan the browser driver acts on. Built from MULTIPLE identities (auth.env): states (pages/resource-states), the actions reachable from each, the transitions those actions drive (under which guard/precondition), and the invariants that must hold — all keyed to the identity/role that can reach them. A modeled flow is CONTEXT, not a finding: it is the substrate the logic/race/authz executors reason over, never proof of a flaw.

version.description: schema version of this context document (current = 1). Optional and backward-compatible (mirrors coverage_ledger.map_version).

identities.description: the accounts/roles the model is keyed to (>=2 so reachability + role-gated transitions can be differenced; +admin for vertical flows). Mirrors authz_context.identities.

states.description: the application states/pages: a node in the app state machine. Each carries the actions reachable from it and which identities observed it. The url/route fields double as the browser driver's navigation plan.

kind.description: the sort of state this node represents

url.description: the URL / route that renders this state (the browser driver navigates here)

reachable_by.description: identity labels observed to reach this state (empty / 'anonymous' = pre-auth)

entry_states.description: state ids a valid flow arrives here from (for step-skip / forced-browsing reasoning)

actions.description: the actions available from this state (the executors tamper/replay/race these)

handler.description: server handler / function name when known (white-box)

allowed_roles.description: identity labels / roles the server is supposed to let perform it (BFLA / vertical surface)

state_change.description: true if the action mutates server state (the race / logic / CSRF surface)

single_use.description: the action is meant to succeed at most once per subject (coupon redeem, withdraw, confirm) — the race-condition over-redemption surface

ui_selector.description: optional selector / control hint so the browser driver can trigger the action in-page

non_replayable.description: the action rides a non-curl-constructible request (e.g. a Next.js / RSC server action: POST + Next-Action header + bound-state multipart body). The consuming executor must SOURCE + REPLAY it from proxy-context/http_history.json, not synthesize it (see _contract/proxy.md).

transitions.description: edges of the state machine: an action drives a move from one state to another, allowed only when its guard holds. The business-logic / auth-bypass executors probe whether the guard is actually enforced server-side; the browser driver walks these to reach deep states.

via.description: the action id that drives this transition

guard.description: the precondition that must hold for the transition to be legitimate, in plain language (e.g. 'payment confirmed', 'owns the resource', 'prior step completed', 'within quota')

guard_kind.description: the class of guard, so executors route it (missing auth/role/ownership -> auth-bypass/idor; sequence/state-precondition/quota -> business-logic; single-use under concurrency -> race-condition)

enforced_by.description: where the guard is observed to be enforced. client-only is a lead: the transition may be reachable by forced browsing / direct request.

taken_by.description: identity labels observed to legitimately take this transition

invariants.description: the rules the application assumes hold across the model — the properties the logic/race/authz executors try to BREAK for impact. An invariant is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.

statement.description: the rule in plain language, e.g. 'an order can be paid at most once', 'price = sum(item.price * qty)', 'only the owner can read a document', 'quota >= 0'

scope_actions.description: action ids whose abuse could violate it

break_impact.description: the concrete impact if it breaks (money, access, data, quota) — so the executor rates severity to the real effect

route.description: the executor best placed to prove a violation of this invariant

flows.description: named multi-step workflows (checkout, registration, password-reset, transfer, upgrade) as an ordered walk over states/actions — the step-skipping / forced-browsing / replay surface, and the browser driver's scripted path to a deep state.

enforced_order.description: true if steps are supposed to run strictly in order (the step-skip surface when the server does not enforce it)

keyed_to.description: identity labels / roles this flow is modeled for

steps.description: ordered steps; each references a state and (optionally) the action that advances it

note.description: what this step contributes / the precondition it establishes

identity_requirements.description: what identities the downstream logic/race/authz hunts actually need, scoped up front (mirrors authz_context). Flags surfaces untestable without operator-provisioned identities (verified/eID/KYC/second-tenant) so the gap is explicit, not discovered mid-hunt.

min_identities.description: how many distinct accounts the deep flows need (>=2)

verification_level.description: entitlement/verification an account needs to reach the sensitive flow (e.g. verified-email / KYC / paid-tier)

untestable_without.description: surfaces blocked until the operator provisions these (e.g. a second verified tenant)
